findings.expected_vs_actual: Strategy coherence: the re-raise spots fold a large share of the hero's own opening range to a single 3-bet even though the price is about 6.5-to-1 (e.g. UTG opens 16.0% but continues only 9.7% in UTG re-raise; folded opens include 66, 55, A9s-A2s, KTs, QTs, T9s, KJo, ATo; CO opens 27.0% vs 11.8% continue). The UTG/HJ re-raise justifications say hands we opened 'usually call one more bet' unless dominated, which the grid contradicts for small pairs and suited aces. Because TAG never open-limps, the re-raise spot is almost always 'we opened and were 3-bet' for the TAG bot.
findings.fix: Non-blocking; for the user's chart review / TASK-6.16 retune or the Q-4 spike: either widen re-raise continues toward the opening ranges (pairs, suited aces, suited connectors) or reword the justifications to state the deliberately tight fold-to-3-bet policy.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Two justifications describe only the common route into a spot: SB blind-defence says 'the big blind is still behind us', but the spot also covers the SB completing and the BB raising; HJ raise says 'The under-the-gun player opened', but HJ also faces a single raise after limping when a later seat raises and everyone else folds.
findings.fix: Optional wording tweak to cover the secondary route.

findings.expected_vs_actual: BB blind-defence marks K9o as a borderline call (alternative fold) and K8o as a borderline fold, while the weaker Q9o, J9o and T8o are firm calls.
findings.fix: Optional: make K9o at least as firm a call as Q9o.
